title_o: On the additive effects of stimulus quality and word frequency in lexical decision: Evidence for opposing interactive influences revealed by RT distributional analyses.
verdict_reason: The audit script reads the first sheet (Sheet3) of YapMu.xlsx (guid 6kaw2): 71 participants x 4 condition mean RTs, and runs a 2x2 within ANOVA; the recomputed quality x frequency interaction F(1,70)=11.78, p=.0010, partial eta^2=.144 matches the table, and the sums of squares equal the ones hard-coded in the script (115052.2 / 683497.9).

data_files.notes: Sheet3 (first in workbook, the one the script reads): per-participant mean RT for Highfrequencyclear, Lowfrequencyclear, Highfrequencydegraded, Lowfrequencydegraded; no NA. Other sheets: Sheet1 trial-level (11,816 rows, 71 subjects), Sheet2 trial-level with procedure names (22,481 rows), Sheet4 an instruction-file text, Sheet5 a long-form copy.
SPSS output viewer file, proprietary; not opened

key_test.test: ez::ezANOVA, within quality (clear/degraded) x frequency (high/low), key statistic = interaction (row 3)

recompute.method: python recomputation (interaction contrast one-sample t, F = t^2, SS from contrast)

obstacles: the step from trial-level RTs (Sheet1/Sheet2) to the condition means in Sheet3 (trimming via the z column) is not scripted
script depends on sheet order (read.xlsx(file,1)) and positional factor labels; needs xlsx, gdata, tidyr, ez (not installed)
